title: Trajectory hiring notes — Eliot Sanchez
content:
Quick personal scratchpad after loop with Eliot Sanchez (phone screen + onsite loop scheduled for next week). Use this to shape the panel brief and the take-home. Not intended to be polished; keep quick heuristics and open questions.

Context: candidate sourced via referral from Rajesh. Background: 6.5 years total, spent last 3 at a mid-size infra startup working on model-serving glue (request orchestration, KV cache, and light-weight runtime optimizations). Prior experience includes C++ infra and Python orchestration. Applied to Sr. Runtime Engineer role focusing on model kernels, batching, and low-latency routing.

Immediate impressions (first 20–30m, phone):
- Communicates clearly, pragmatic. Picks a single approach and defends tradeoffs rather than flitting between ideas.
- Strong intuition for tail-latency causes (cold-KV fetch, context-switching on worker threads) — had a crisp example where they reduced tail p95 by ~25% by changing work-stealing policy + request coalescing.
- Not super deep on recent attention-kernel research (e.g., flash attention internals), but understands the systems-level implications and knows when to pair with ML/kernel experts.

Strengths (to call out in scorecard):
- Ownership mindset: ran a small infra team of 2–3, shipped SLA-backed micro-services for customers.
- Good debugging heuristics for production RTT issues: latency flamegraphs, queueing theory intuition, and pragmatic sampling for KV hits.
- Comfortable in mixed-language stacks (C++ core + Python orchestration).

Risks / unknowns:
- Kernel-level optimization chops are moderate but not stellar; has limited experience with custom CUDA kernels or Triton. Could be slower to land deep kernel improvements without pairing.
- Limited exposure to large-scale A/B rollout patterns (they've done canary + basic metric checks but not multivariate traffic shaping).
- Not tested on quantization/INT8 workflows — unknown whether they can evaluate quality vs perf tradeoffs.

Behavioral / culture fit notes:
- Pragmatic, prefers shipping iteratively. Connects to our production-first ethos.
- Good collaborator stories — cited a time negotiating rollout windows with data science and SRE to avoid customer impact.

Suggested technical questions for onsite loop (targeting gaps):
1) Deep debugging scenario: present a synthetic workload where p99 spikes after a release — ask them to walk from hypothesis to remediation (include metrics: request queue length, CPU steal, GC events, KV hit-rate). Aim to see systemic troubleshooting + mitigation steps.
2) Batching and latency tradeoff exercise: given mix of short (8-token) & long (2048-token) requests, how would they architect batching to meet 95th percentile latency SLO while preserving throughput? Watch for cache prefixing and pre-emptive flushing ideas.
3) Kernel-collaboration prompt: ask to design an experiment to determine whether to invest in a custom kernel or algorithmic change at orchestration layer. Expect cost-benefit framing, measurable success criteria.

Quick heuristics / rough numeric score (for my own use):
- Technical depth (systems/runtime): 7/10
- Kernel/specialized ML optimization: 5/10
- Product/ownership: 8/10
- Cross-team communication: 8/10
- Overall hireability (stretch Sr IC): strong yes for senior infra engineer, marginal for principal runtime kernel lead.

Comp band anchor (for recruiter): competitive mid-senior range. If we want kernel-heavy role, need to price higher or pair with kernel growth plan.

Follow-ups / action items (short):
- Draft onsite loop that includes one kernel-savvy interviewer (ask Rajesh if he can cover kernel/attention internals).
- Create a 90-min take-home option focusing on batching design (if candidate prefers take-home). Keep it pragmatic: metric-driven, not pure implementation.
- Ask candidate pre-onsite to send a short doc (bullet points) about the biggest production incident they've owned and the key metrics they watched.

Open questions to resolve before panel:
- Actual depth of CUDA/Trition experience? (flag for phone follow-up).
- Recent latency numbers they've owned (p50/p95/p99 ranges) and traffic scale.
- Availability for start date and comp expectations.

Notes-to-self:
- Keep onboarding plan in mind: if hired, propose initial 30–60–90 with pairing on batcher, prefix cache, and one perf project that yields measurable $/token improvement.
- Flag as potential mentor pair for junior runtime hires if technical coaching & ownership are priorities.

Random snippets I said during phone: 
- "I value people who can reduce cost without sacrificing latency — that tight tradeoff is everywhere here."
- "If you like colos and kernel work, we do have folks focused there; if you prefer higher-level orchestration we can position you on that axis."

End of scratchpad. Revisit after onsite and update this doc with panel feedback.
